# Agent Decision Reduction Profile: Causa Rehearsal and Competition

**AR-001 [P0] Source-of-truth baseline.** Every run must pin authoritative requirements and their source repository, commit, and content digest. A modified baseline must be detected and require an authorized change process.

**AR-002 [P0] Lossless requirement derivation.** Each source obligation must have a machine-verifiable mapping to an implementation requirement, or a recorded scope disposition. Detect omissions, weakening, negation, and role/value swaps, not only literal missing strings.

**AR-003 [P0] Authenticated decisions.** Agents must not approve their own exclusions, waivers, acceptance, or architectural exceptions. Require verifiable operator or delegated-authority approval, bound to the exact requirement and baseline digest.

**AR-004 [P0] Mandatory CI preservation gate.** A required, non-optional job must verify baseline integrity, requirement coverage, approvals, and evidence before merge or acceptance. Failing, missing, skipped, or bypassed checks cannot be reported PASS.

**AR-005 [P0] Capability registry and reuse.** Before designing a component, discover existing Echelon capabilities, owners, supported versions, and contracts. Reuse verified implementations; require an explicit approved justification for duplication.

**AR-006 [P0] Typed state and transition contracts.** Represent valid states, permissions, and transitions with typed F# contracts where practical. Invalid or unauthorized transitions must be rejected before side effects.

**AR-007 [P0] Evidence-backed acceptance.** Every PASS must cite the actual test, assertion, artifact, environment, and source SHA. Distinguish PASS, FAIL, PARTIAL, BLOCKED, and NOT_RUN; never infer PASS from code presence or a mock result.

**AR-008 [P0] Adversarial independent review.** A reviewer distinct from the implementer must attempt to falsify high-risk claims, inspect requirements and evidence, and record gaps. Reviewers cannot self-ratify operator decisions.

**AR-009 [P0] Negative-control testing.** Critical tests must include a deliberately invalid case that fails for the intended reason. Detect tests that pass regardless of implementation or verify mere existence rather than behavior.

**AR-010 [P0] Layered provider verification.** Run fast deterministic domain/fixture tests frequently, provider contract tests at integration boundaries, and real provider and deployed browser tests at acceptance. Live tests must never silently substitute mocks.

**AR-011 [P0] Reproducibility and provenance.** Record tool versions, pinned dependency SHAs, fixture seeds and digests, build inputs, CI run IDs, and deployed SHA. Re-run must distinguish reproducible differences from environment drift.

**AR-012 [P0] Controlled work scope.** Agent changes must be bounded to named requirements and paths; commits should stage intended files only. Detect unrelated changes and require explicit review before inclusion.

**AR-013 [P0] Risk-based verification.** Select tests based on changed contracts and dependency impact, preserving mandatory security, integrity, and release gates. Batching tests for efficiency cannot bypass required checks.

**AR-014 [P0] Secure capability isolation.** Agents receive only the credentials, repository access, context, and mutation permissions required for current work. Never echo secrets in logs, prompts, screenshots, or test artifacts.

**AR-015 [P0] Long-running agent continuity.** Maintain durable, compact, machine-readable checkpoints of objectives, decisions, completed work, open defects, evidence, and next actions so agent restarts do not re-decide settled questions.

**AR-016 [P1] Reliability experiment.** Compare existing agent workflow with constrained workflow on matched tasks, recording correctness, requirement retention, false PASS rate, rework, elapsed time, and token usage. Preserve raw evidence, define acceptance metrics before the run, and do not treat unobserved gains as measured.

**AR-017 [P0] Ownership and intake.** Route implementation work to the actual owning repository through its documented Praxis input folder and accepted grammar, never GitHub Issues. Do not assume component ownership from its name.

**AR-018 [P0] Fail-closed acceptance.** Missing credentials, unavailable external verification, unsigned approvals, stale evidence, failed gates, or unverified deployed artifacts must produce BLOCKED or FAIL as appropriate. An agent cannot override these outcomes with narrative.

**AR-019 [P0] Computed verdict, not agent assertion.** The authoritative acceptance outcome MUST be computed from the evidence ledger, frozen baseline, required gates, requirements coverage, approved decisions, defect closures, and deployed SHA. Agent-authored accepted fields are advisory at most. Original Rehearsal 3 must yield BLOCKED; Rehearsal 2 candidate 45644a7 should yield ACCEPTED only if its actual ledger and evidence meet the frozen contract. Include tests for false accepted flags, missing CI, baseline tampering, and unauthorized waivers.

**AR-020 [P0] Selective enforcement.** Retain the demonstrated four-tier architecture brief as default guidance. Do not add per-step Ordo architecture enforcement, typed agent records, or executable decision gates without a measured incremental correctness benefit that justifies cost and false rejections. Typed domain models and security/acceptance boundaries remain mandatory where independently justified.

**AR-021 [P0] Continuous implementation agent.** Prefer one long-running implementation agent with compact durable checkpoints. Do not require structured handoffs by default. Measure correctness and requirement retention after context compaction; use independent reviewers at release candidates.

**AR-022 [P0] Testing discipline.** Dependency-based test selection may prioritize but must not omit mandatory regression/security/integration coverage. Do not restrict CI to infrequent checkpoints when intermediate changes can hide failures. Require baseline tests that demonstrably fail on injected defects before trusting an experiment.

**AR-023 [P0] Release-set integrity.** Select the latest *verified compatible release set*, not unrelated latest versions. Confirm whether Dokimos 0.7.0 and Percepta have published artifacts; do not claim attestation from a set lacking its required components. Resolve and verify Conditor scaffold defect SD-1. Pin the exact set and require evidence for waivers.

**AR-024 [P0] Explicit kickoff decisions.** An authorized human must resolve the write scope, Percepta release/waiver, DF-CAUSA-2026-0003 operator decisions, and frozen requirements/stack before a timed full-write rehearsal. Agents must not self-ratify these decisions.

**AR-025 [P1] Research controls.** Compare constrained versus baseline workflows on matched tasks with measured accepted requirements, false acceptance, escaped defects, token cost, elapsed time, and rework. Do not claim 'prevented by design' without a falsifiable test or generalize a single reviewer observation as proven efficacy.

**AR-026 [P1] Shared HTTP cache.** Investigate a provider-neutral, opt-in cache policy at the Limen HTTP boundary with explicit freshness, invalidation, security, and stale-data semantics; do not silently use stale results for authoritative decisions. Place implementation in Limen's documented Praxis input path after owner/contract verification.

- EXT-DATA-001 [P0] The application source, test assets included in production, release artifacts, Pages deployment, and runtime bundle MUST NOT contain the five R001 demonstration investigation datasets, event histories, golden states, or other prepopulated investigation content. The data contract, schema definitions, type declarations, command/event catalog, migration rules, and synthetic test generators MAY be included; synthetic tests MUST NOT ship production records.

- EXT-DATA-002 [P0] A fresh launch MUST display an accessible empty/disconnected workspace and an explicit Connect data repository action. No implicit demo import or automatic fallback to bundled fixtures is allowed.

- EXT-DATA-003 [P0] The user MUST specify or explicitly select the repository and permitted branch/workspace, and provide a scoped credential through a secure connection flow. A token alone is not sufficient to infer a safe repository target.

- EXT-DATA-004 [P0] Credentials MUST never be committed, bundled, logged, embedded in URLs, exposed in error text, stored in localStorage, or written into domain event files. Prefer short-lived least-privilege tokens or GitHub App authorization. In-memory-only credentials require reauthorization after reload. Do not use an unrestricted personal access token by default.

- EXT-DATA-005 [P0] The GitHub provider MUST check repository and branch permissions, validate file paths and manifests, and load only schema-compatible data through the full contract validation and F# history-admissibility pipeline. Malformed, forged, unauthorized, or incompatible data MUST fail closed with safe diagnostics.

- EXT-DATA-006 [P0] No data or repository mutation occurs on connect or read. Creating a new investigation is an explicit user action; write/publish requires separately verified authorization, optimistic concurrency, and no overwrite of unread remote history.

- EXT-DATA-007 [P0] The UI MUST distinguish disconnected, connecting, authorized-empty, loading, incompatible, access-denied, offline, and conflict states. Never imply a successful connection merely because a token was supplied.

- EXT-DATA-008 [P0] The app MUST create new Causa v1 file sets from the authoritative schema and engine without copying a demo investigation. A new empty investigation MUST be command-created, schema-validated, replayable, and round-trip verified.

- EXT-DATA-009 [P0] Build and acceptance tests MUST demonstrate a clean install with zero production investigation fixtures, no preloaded investigation records, successful authorized retrieval from a separately populated test repository, denial without authorization, malformed-data refusal, and successful create/read/write/reload. The deployed exact SHA must be verified.

- EXT-DATA-010 [P0] R001 remains an immutable experimental baseline. The next rehearsal MUST measure external-data startup, authorization, read, write, and recovery independently. Do not claim an external provider PASS based on mocked requests alone.

- EXT-DATA-011 [P0] Preserve compatibility with the frozen Causa storage contract as a *reader/writer specification* without vendoring its demonstration records. Version the contract and fail closed on incompatible data.

- EXT-DATA-012 [P0] The data repository MUST be configurable and isolated from the application repository. Treat repository content as untrusted even when authenticated. Do not grant data access through publicly readable Pages assets.

- EXT-DATA-013 [P0] The active demonstration catalog is the one named by causa-data `catalog/active.json` (historical-v1): exactly three historical investigations, Apollo 1 (AS-204), Apollo 11 and Space Shuttle Challenger (STS-51-L). After an explicit Connect to that repository and workspace, the application MUST load all three through the full contract validation and F# replay pipeline to the states recorded in the catalog manifest, MUST NOT present any synthetic investigation as a catalog case, and MUST NOT bundle any of their records. The five synthetic v1.0.0 fixtures remain the storage contract's test corpus only (STORAGE-005, STORAGE-007).
# Frozen Demo Data and Storage Compatibility Requirements

**PF-001 [P0] Provider-neutral boundary.** Define a typed F# investigation-data port shared by fixture and GitHub adapters. The application/UI must consume the same result, error, cancellation, freshness, and provenance semantics regardless of provider. Provider selection must not alter domain meaning or authorization.

**PF-002 [P0] One domain authority.** Fixture adapters supply contract-compliant inputs; they must not implement parallel domain policy, state transitions, event reconstruction, causal inference, or confidence calculations. The existing F# engine validates and reconstructs both fixture and real-provider data.

**PF-003 [P0] Explicit provider selection.** Support an explicit local fixture mode and real GitHub mode, using a documented, repeatable build/run/test command (FAKE or equivalent). Fixture mode must require no network access, GitHub credentials, database, or external service. It must not silently activate in a production deployment. Display the active data mode conspicuously and never imply fixture data is live.

**PF-004 [P0] Contract fidelity.** Fixture data must follow the frozen versioned Causa storage contract and be loaded through the same parsing/validation/reconstruction path as real data. Maintain a machine-readable fixture manifest with IDs, schema versions, expected domain versions/digests, and expected error outcomes. Do not mutate the frozen historical dataset.

**PF-005 [P0] Provider isolation.** UI and domain tests must not directly depend on GitHub, GitHub Actions, network availability, or credentials. Real-provider tests must not silently fall back to fixtures or report mocked results as live success.

**PF-006 [P0] Populated investigation.** Supply a compact complete investigation with observations, competing hypotheses, supporting and contradicting evidence, provenance, unknowns, causal relationships, corrective actions, verification records, timeline events, and populated semantic color states. Use stable IDs, timestamps, and deterministic ordering.

**PF-007 [P0] Edge-case fixtures.** Supply an empty investigation; a completed/verified investigation; missing or incomplete provenance; unresolved and contradictory evidence; invalid event history; invalid schema; malformed or missing catalog; and missing investigation. Expected outcomes must be explicit, including fail-closed behavior.

**PF-008 [P0] Provider-failure fixtures.** Model authorization failure, forbidden access, not found, missing branch (including GitHub HTTP 422 where observed), rate limit, timeout, offline failure, malformed response, retry, and partial transport failure. Distinguish provider errors from domain validation errors.

**PF-009 [P0] Concurrency fixtures.** Deterministically schedule delayed, reordered, superseded, cancelled, and retried requests. A stale response must never overwrite the state of a newer request, and cached success must never mask a new authentication failure. Request identity, active provider, credential generation, and freshness must be honored.

**PF-010 [P1] Fixture maintainability.** Provide a small, representative default dataset for rapid development plus opt-in extended scenarios. Avoid large duplicated JSON fixtures and ensure fixture edits are reviewed as contract changes.

**PF-012 [P0] Fast local feedback.** Document a single command that builds and starts a populated fixture-backed UI and a separate command for fast offline domain/UI/provider-contract checks. CI must run offline deterministic checks without secrets. Record execution time and failures by layer; set measurable performance budgets after baseline measurement rather than inventing targets.

**PF-013 [P0] Real-provider conformance.** Maintain sanitized, versioned observations of actual GitHub status codes, response bodies, relevant headers, branch behavior, pagination, cache behavior, and retry semantics. Tests must detect fake/real divergence. Do not capture secrets, private payloads, or sensitive headers. Refresh observations when the provider contract changes.

**PF-014 [P0] Live integration acceptance.** At defined integration checkpoints and before release acceptance, run a real GitHub provider test against the approved repository and pinned catalog. Confirm actual network communication, correct request-to-response association, three historical investigation reconstructions, expected versions/digests, and deployed application behavior. Record repository ref, source SHA, run ID, and provider mode. Never claim live success from mocks.

**PF-015 [P0] Credentials and security.** Public read-only catalog tests should not require a PAT when anonymous access is sufficient. Authenticated integration tests use an approved secret such as `CAUSA_GITHUB_TOKEN` when explicitly required, with least-privilege read-only permissions. Never embed or print credentials, put them in URLs, or include them in screenshots, traces, logs, or artifacts. A missing secret yields BLOCKED, not PASS.

**PF-016 [P0] Visual verification.** Fixture scenarios must exercise navy, teal, amber, coral, and ivory per UI-016, with textual state labels and contrast checks. Capture deployed exact-SHA screenshots at required desktop, iPad, and mobile sizes for final acceptance; local fixture screenshots alone do not satisfy deployed acceptance.

**PF-017 [P0] Failure isolation.** Report failures by domain, UI, provider contract, or live integration layer. A provider outage must not make offline UI/domain checks fail; an offline pass must not waive a failing integration gate.

**PF-018 [P0] Traceability.** Map each fixture and test to stable requirements and authoritative source commit. Preserve obligations during rehearsal derivation; missing or weakened P0 obligations must fail requirements reconciliation unless explicitly approved as out of scope.

**PF-019 [P0] Local-first workflow.** During development, agents should run the smallest relevant deterministic tests first, batch integration checks at meaningful checkpoints, and run the complete live/deployed suite before release. Never skip a test required by an impacted risk or dependency.

**PF-020 [P0] Deployment gate.** Release acceptance requires green domain, fixture UI, provider conformance, and applicable live integration checks, plus exact-SHA deployed browser verification. If the live provider or required credential is unavailable, report BLOCKED and preserve offline test evidence.

**PF-021 [P1] Reusable implementation.** Implement provider-neutral contracts and test harnesses in the narrowest appropriate Echelon components, avoiding a Causa-only parallel framework and minimizing dependencies. Keep fixture definitions and application-specific scenarios with the application.

**VER-001 [P0] Latest compatible verified release.** Each build MUST use the newest available stable, published, compatible release of every applicable Echelon system at the time the build baseline is locked. Applicable systems include Praxis, Ordo, Dokimos, Percepta, Forma, Forma Studio/workflow layout, Limen, Folio, and any actually integrated Echelon dependencies. Discover the real owner and release channel for each; do not invent a release or assume every system is a runtime dependency.

**VER-002 [P0] Verify release freshness.** Query authoritative package registries, GitHub releases/tags, or the owning repository's documented release source immediately before baseline lock. Record checked timestamp, candidate release, source reference, and why it was selected. Do not equate latest main commit with latest released artifact.

**VER-003 [P0] Compatibility over blind upgrades.** Prefer latest stable only when integration contracts and acceptance tests pass. If the newest release is incompatible, fail the upgrade gate or obtain a documented, authorized exception for the newest known compatible release. Never silently fall back to an old version.

**VER-004 [P0] Reproducible lock.** Pin exact package versions and immutable artifact digests/commit SHAs in a machine-readable dependency manifest. The lock is fixed for a given rehearsal/run and must not drift mid-run. Re-resolve latest versions for each new rehearsal or explicitly authorized refresh.

**VER-005 [P0] No unreviewed prereleases.** Do not adopt alpha, beta, RC, unpublished source, or unverified local builds merely because they are newer. Such use requires explicit approval, provenance, and the same compatibility and security gates.

**VER-006 [P0] Cross-system contract validation.** Verify supported API/schema compatibility across Praxis, Ordo, Dokimos, Percepta, Forma, workflow layout, Limen, Folio, and other applicable systems. Exercise integration tests, not just version-string comparisons. Include the local bootstrap/build path and deployed browser where applicable.

**VER-007 [P0] Version observability.** Show resolved application, dependency, and build versions in Administration (UI-018), not investigation pages, catalog cards, or the global footer. Versions must reflect actual loaded components rather than aspirational requirements.

**VER-008 [P0] CI enforcement.** A mandatory gate must verify the locked manifest against installed/loaded artifacts and compatibility evidence. Missing dependencies, stale evidence, unverified artifacts, or skipped gates result in BLOCKED/FAIL, not PASS.

**VER-009 [P1] Upgrade impact and rollback.** Record release notes, breaking changes, migration needs, security advisories, rollback target, and tests affected by each upgrade. Keep historical run manifests and evidence immutable.

**VER-010 [P0] Requirements traceability.** Every future rehearsal must reconcile VER-001..VER-010 with implementation and tests or an explicitly approved exclusion. Work items must go through each owning repository's documented Praxis input path, not GitHub Issues.

**WDL-001 [P0] Existing capability discovery.** Identify the workflow layout engine's owning repository, supported package or source integration, API, version, license, and constraints before implementation. Document evidence of a working example and identify any required upstream changes.

**WDL-002 [P0] No duplicate engine.** Causa must not introduce a second general-purpose graph layout implementation or maintain fixed SVG coordinates for domain nodes and edges when the existing workflow engine supports them. An explicitly documented temporary fallback requires approval and cannot be represented as satisfying this requirement.

**WDL-003 [P0] Typed domain-to-graph projection.** Define a typed F# adapter that projects authoritative causal assertions, outcomes, hypotheses, cause roles (root cause, trigger, contributing factor, enabling condition), and evidence counts into graph nodes and relationships. The projection must not invent causal claims, change domain states, or perform domain inference.

**WDL-004 [P0] Separation of concerns.** Causa owns graph semantics; the reusable workflow system owns placement, routing, spacing, and supported layout constraints; Forma owns accessible visual components and semantic styling. Keep these responsibilities independently testable.

**WDL-005 [P0] Data-driven layout.** Node placement and edge geometry must be computed from graph input and supported constraints, not from hardcoded coordinates for specific investigations. Layout must remain valid for zero, one, many, disconnected, and cyclic graphs where the domain permits them.

**WDL-006 [P0] Visual correctness.** Layout must avoid unintended node overlaps, clipped labels, inaccessible connectors, and hidden evidence counts. Edge crossings and visual ambiguity should be minimized using documented layout capabilities; do not promise zero crossings for arbitrary graphs.

**WDL-007 [P0] Responsive and accessible rendering.** Support desktop, iPad portrait/landscape, and mobile with accessible text equivalents, meaningful labels, keyboard navigation/focus, adequate contrast, zoom/reflow or intentional navigable overflow, and reduced-motion preferences. Diagram information must not depend on color alone.

**WDL-008 [P0] Forma design-system alignment.** Render graph nodes and statuses using Forma-compatible components/tokens and the canonical Causa UI-016 semantic palette. Colors must reflect domain-authoritative states; layout cannot assign causal or evidentiary meaning.

**WDL-009 [P0] Stable and deterministic output.** Given identical graph data, layout engine version, viewport constraints, and configuration, output must be deterministic within documented tolerances. Stable node IDs and ordering must survive refreshes; avoid needless visual movement.

**WDL-010 [P0] Interaction contract.** Where the workflow component supports interaction, node selection and navigation must resolve to authoritative investigation records. Read-only rehearsal scope must not expose editing, drag-to-modify-domain, or persistence capabilities without explicit authorization.

**WDL-011 [P0] Fixture-backed development.** Include deterministic graph fixtures: empty, single-node, four cause roles, dense evidence, long labels, disconnected graph, and permitted cycles. The fixture provider must use the same domain-to-graph projection as the real GitHub provider (PF-001..PF-021).

**WDL-012 [P0] Layered tests.** Independently test graph projection, layout invariants, rendering/accessibility, and live integration. Verify expected nodes, roles, relationships, evidence counts, no unintended overlap or clipping, stable output, keyboard/text-equivalent access, and real historical investigation rendering.

**WDL-013 [P1] Comparative experiment.** Compare the existing fixed-coordinate SVG approach against the reusable workflow layout system on identical causal graphs. Record layout correctness, overlap, clipping, edge crossings, responsiveness, implementation effort, test effort, and agent token consumption. Hold graph data and acceptance criteria constant; preserve original measurements and distinguish observed results from estimates.

**WDL-014 [P0] Integration gate.** Before claiming completion, prove the application actually invokes the identified workflow layout capability, records the pinned dependency version/SHA, and passes fixture, accessibility, and deployed-browser tests. A visually similar hand-coded diagram is not equivalent.

**WDL-015 [P0] Requirements preservation.** Every future rehearsal requirements package must trace WDL-001..WDL-015 to implementation and verification or record an explicitly approved scope exclusion. Do not silently omit these obligations during derivation.
